Irene / Ben — draft language and comments below. I'm keeping items short so you can paste into the order-form/exhibit.

1) Outputs / IP:
Proposed clause: "Customer retains all right, title and interest in and to Customer Data and Customer Output. 'Customer Output' means text, images or other content generated by the Service in response to Customer Data or prompts submitted by Customer. Redwood shall have no ownership or rights to Customer Output and shall not use Customer Output to improve or train models without Customer's prior written consent."
Comment: this is standard for customers with sensitive data. We can add a mutual exception for anonymized, aggregated telemetry used solely for reliability improvements (non-training).

2) Training / Use for model improvement:
Proposed clause: "Redwood may collect usage telemetry and aggregated performance metrics. Unless Customer elects to opt-in, Redwood will not use Customer Data or Customer Output to train models intended for public release or shared model weights."

3) Subprocessors / Order-form exhibit:
Proposed clause: "Redwood may engage subprocessors for hosting and delivery. Redwood will provide Customer with an up-to-date list of subprocessors on request and shall notify Customer of material changes. For regulated Customer Data, Redwood will comply with data residency commitments specified in the Order Form Annex. Customer's audit rights are limited to receipt of SOC/equivalent reports and evidence; on-site audits are subject to mutual agreement and reimbursement."

4) Indemnity and caps:
Response: KeenHealth proposed unlimited indemnity for IP and a higher-than-normal cap tied to annual spend. We should push for a customary mutual IP indemnity plus a liability cap equal to the fees paid by Customer to Redwood in the prior 12 months, with exceptions for willful misconduct and gross negligence.
Proposed clause: "Except for liability arising from (i) willful misconduct or gross negligence, or (ii) Customer's breach of obligations concerning regulated data, Redwood's aggregate liability to Customer shall be limited to the fees paid by Customer to Redwood in the 12 months preceding the claim."

5) PHI / Healthcare considerations:
Note: If KeenHealth will submit PHI, we need a Business Associate Addendum (BAA). We can accommodate BAAs but will require specific scope and technical controls (encryption at rest/in-transit, KMS access controls, logging).

I'll prepare a redlined Word doc for Irene to send. Let me know if Ben has commercial flexibility on the cap.

-Markus
Markus Klein
